SpaceX (SPCX), AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) and Rocket Lab (RKLB) shares fell overnight as fears of political backlash against Elon Musk following Democratic midterm gains spilled into the broader space sector, raising fresh questions about a potential Tesla-SpaceX merger. SPCX, RKLB, ASTS, Planet Labs (PL), Redwire (RDW) and Intuitive Machines (LUNR) all fell between 2% and 6% overnight heading into Wednesday. Democrats won the Senate and are projected to take the House, raising the prospect of tougher scrutiny of Musk’s government dealings. The selling also swept the wider market: Nasdaq futures fell 0.4% and S&P 500 futures slid 0.3%, and Dow futures slipped 0.1% heading into Wednesday trade. Satellite communications and spectrum consultant Tim Farrar raised the prospect of Musk shifting the spotlight from politics to business. “Will Musk/SpaceX announce some business deal tomorrow to change the focus away from politics?” he asked on X. His doubts come after a recent note in which he speculated that SpaceX could pursue EchoStar’s remaining business through a share-based deal involving wireless assets and spectrum. Meanwhile, Alexandra Merz, CEO of L&F Investor Services, questioned Musk’s political spending: “First time I see Elon not making good on the money he invests.” Musk contributed $446 million during the 2026 midterm election cycle, mostly to Republican-aligned groups. Musk’s ties to Trump and his former role leading DOGE have raised the stakes, with Democrats threatening investigations into his government work and federal contracts. Lawmakers have also sought a probe into reported SpaceX communications restrictions in Ukraine. Trump recently signaled willingness to consider pre-emptive pardons for Musk and other allies, saying: “I would if I needed to, sure. I wouldn’t even think about it. I did it for J6.” Merz said Democratic gains could bring more hearings, subpoenas and scrutiny of government contracts, complicating a Tesla-SpaceX merger without automatically blocking it. “Congress cannot simply veto a private merger,” she said. “It does not, by itself, put the merger off the table.” She identified shareholder approval, special-committee processes and regulatory reviews as the key hurdles. Both companies have formed committees to assess a merger. Merz pointed to committee progress, potential disclosures ahead of Tesla’s Dec.3 annual meeting and formal deal terms as the next developments to watch. Veteran investor George Noble urged adding to his bearish bets on Musk’s companies. “Elon Musk is the biggest loser in the elections tonight. TIME to add to our profitable short positions in $SPCX and $TSLA,” he said on X. “The speed of the coming collapse will be something to behold.” Last month, Noble called Tesla and SpaceX short calls at $485 and $145, respectively, pointing to cash burn, heavy spending and high valuations. He acknowledged then that Tesla had fallen since his call, while SpaceX had risen. “The election doesn’t solve the AI funding problem.” Cardone Capital founder and CEO Grant Cardone also flagged political risks: “If talarico wins Texas it won’t be good for SpaceX or the AI bet.” Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton, ending Democrats’ statewide losing streak in Texas dating to 1994. On the other hand, Morgan Stanley offered a bullish counterpoint, as per a note shared by Tesla investor and influencer Sawyer Merritt. “On fiscal year 2028, $SPCX trades cheaper than the S&P500. Interesting,” the firm said. Using a $140 reference share price and projected 2028 adjusted earnings of $109 billion, the research firm put SpaceX at 17.6 times estimated earnings, just below the S&P 500’s estimated 17.7 times multiple. He nearly doubled his 2027 revenue forecast to $175 billion and raised his 2028 revenue and operating-income estimates to $289 billion and $119 billion, respectively. “At the time of our initiation, we had expected SPCX to be FCF negative until 2035. Today, we forecast the company to achieve positive FCF by 2031 - a 4 year pull-forward FCF break-even,” Morgan Stanley said. Projected borrowing fell to $390 billion through 2031 from $670 billion through 2035, though the forecasts cover different periods. On Stocktwits, sentiment for SPCX, ASTS and RKLB was ‘bearish,’ with ‘low’ message activity across all three stocks. One user said, “That’s why EM [Elon Musk] should have stayed out of politics, now you tie your share price to the political landscape.” Another user said that Musk’s critics in a Democratic-led Congress could favor funding and contracts for companies outside his business empire. AST buys SpaceX launch services while competing in satellite-based mobile connectivity. Rocket Lab competes with SpaceX for launches and supplies spacecraft and components to government customers, giving the companies different exposure to Musk’s political risks. A separate user urged investors to hold their positions, citing historically strong market performance in the third year of a presidential term. U.S. President Donald Trump claimed Republicans would have won a landslide had he been on the ballot as Democrats captured the Senate and projected to win the House, while market strategists warned of gridlock and growing risks for AI investors. Election-night nerves turned trading screens red: the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) fell 0.8%, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) lost 1.2% and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) slipped 0.5% overnight heading into Wednesday. The selloff extended to index futures, with Dow futures down 0.3%, S&P 500 futures off 0.6%, and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.8% lower. Trump Media & Technology Group (DJT) also fell overnight, tumbling over 6% to $6.30. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump said on Truth Social as Republican losses mounted Tuesday. The claim followed his appeal just days earlier for supporters to treat the midterms as a vote on his presidency. At a weekend rally in Dubuque, Iowa, he told voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” putting his leadership at the heart of the campaign. Democrats secured Senate control after flipping Republican-held seats in six states. Roy Cooper won in North Carolina, James Talarico in Texas, Annie Andrews in South Carolina, Sherrod Brown in Ohio, Adam Hamilton in Kansas and Josh Turek in Iowa. The party was also projected to win a House majority, putting Democrats in position to challenge Trump’s agenda across both chambers. Counting continues, with final seat totals still unsettled. Before posting his landslide claim, Trump struck a more conciliatory tone in a late-Tuesday interview. “I am absolutely willing to accept those results,” he said, expressing willingness to cooperate with Democrats and adding: “We’ll probably work something out.” World Trade Securities CEO Nicholas Mugalli warned about the election’s potential market fallout. “Tonight is an absolute bloodbath for all investors especially AI investors,” he said on X. Mugalli pointed to Texas’ importance as a hub for AI data centers, warning that Democratic gains could bring tougher regulation. He also criticized Trump’s handling of inflation and living costs. Carson Group Chief Market Strategist Ryan Detrick raised broader concerns about the prospect of a Republican president facing a Democratic Congress. “The worst possible combination is a Republican President and a Democratic Congress. Futures seem to agree so far,” he said on X. GLJ Research analyst Gordon Johnson called the Democratic Senate takeover a surprise, saying the Washington consultants he follows had either viewed control as a toss-up or expected Republicans to hold the chamber. “NONE of them predicted the Democrats would take the Senate,” he said on X. “No matter what ANYONE tells you, this is 100% a surprise.” Other forecasters had seen a stronger Democratic outlook. Before the vote, polling analyst Nate Silver’s model gave the party an 80% chance of winning the Senate, while his election-day analysis called Democrats clear favorites for the House. Silver linked Republicans’ troubles to Trump’s unpopularity, the Iran war, fuel prices and public anxiety about AI data centers. “All of these problems are Trump’s fault. He almost seems to have a death wish in these midterms,” Silver said before the results. Historian Allan Lichtman also anticipated big Democratic gains. “I am expecting a net gain of 40 U.S. House and 6 U.S. Senate seats. Let’s see how close we get,” he said on X. Infowars founder Alex Jones portrayed Republican losses as a major blow to Trump’s political coalition. In an X post, he quoted Richard Baris, a pollster and managing director of Big Data Poll: “This Is A Beating That Will Keep Republicans Out Of The Senate For 10 Years!” Jones added: “THE TRUMP COALITION HAS BEEN OBLITERATED!” Meanwhile, economist Peter Schiff saw a different consequence: Democratic victories could give Trump someone to blame if the economy deteriorates. “Since the Democrats swept the midterms, Trump has the scapegoat he needs for the coming economic collapse,” Schiff wrote on X, calling the outcome a sweep. Former Goldman Sachs strategist Robin Brooks turned to the potential fallout beyond Washington, questioning whether Democratic gains could increase the likelihood of renewed fighting with Iran. “I think it raises the odds of war,” he said. Brooks also linked the risk to the outlook for oil and precious metals. James Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus, said that a divided government could preserve much of Trump’s economic agenda, even as it makes new legislation harder to pass. “If Democrats control the House and Senate with a Republican president, the Hamiltonian economic agenda stays largely intact,” he said. “Gridlock freezes the existing framework.” Thorne said existing tax provisions, production incentives and tariffs would be difficult to unwind. He viewed the election as a demand to tackle affordability and end the Iran conflict. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Joby Aviation (JOBY) stock is drawing attention ahead of its third-quarter (Q3) earnings as ARK Invest analyst Tasha Keeney sees autonomous electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft eventually offering fares competitive with traditional taxis. Joby Aviation stock traded over 2% lower overnight, heading into Wednesday. The stock has been declining for the past five months. In an X post, ARK Invest analyst Daniel Maguire recalled how St. Petersburg hosted the first commercial airline journey in 1914. Pilot Tony Jannus carried former St. Petersburg Mayor Abram Fail to Tampa Bay in about 23 minutes. Fail paid $400 for the trip, equivalent to more than $10,000 in 2026 dollars. The experimental airline service operated for three months, giving the industry important lessons about running commercial flights. More than a century later, the same Florida waterfront hosted a demonstration of an electric aircraft developed by Joby Aviation. Keeney said a drive that normally requires about 45 minutes took the aircraft less than half that time. The demonstration offered an early look at how electric aircraft could change short-distance transportation, particularly in cities where road travel frequently slows down. “In the future, we expect that eVTOLs that are autonomously operated could price competitively with today's human-driven taxi cabs.” She also pointed to the possibility of widespread ground-based robotaxis, which could reduce transportation costs per mile but potentially increase the number of vehicles on roads. If cheaper autonomous rides lead to heavier traffic, journeys that already take 45 minutes could become even longer. Keeney added that electric aircraft could benefit from that situation by offering passengers a way to avoid busy roads while reaching their destinations in considerably less time. Last week, ARK Invest made a string of JOBY share purchases through two of its exchange-traded funds (ETFs), ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) and ARK Space Exploration & Innovation ETF (ARKX), signaling conviction in the company’s commercial flight trials. Joby has gained momentum following its active involvement in the FAA’s Electric Powered-lift Integration Program (eIPP).  The company’s second-quarter revenue jumped 56% to $39 million. Joby will report its Q3 earnings on Nov. 4. Analysts expect $40.42 million in revenue and a loss of $0.25 per share, according to Fiscal.ai.
